title: Swap, Replicate, Read the Mass: A Protocol for Auditing Demographic Bias in System One Decision Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.00496v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: System One decision models replace text generation with typed, probability-scored answers and are entering production. Answers execute without a person in the loop, and no multi-model audit exists on established bias benchmarks. We provide that audit: three benchmarks: BBQ (all eleven categories), CrowS-Pairs, and SilverSpoon, adapted to the typed interface, twelve models plus a no-thinking ablation, and 1,638,000 decisions. Every order-sensitive item runs twice with options swapped; native typed models also swap labels; ten configurations repeat under extra seeds and batch 16. We find widespread stereotype alignment, order-dependent answers, and confidence that tracks instability rather than bias. In BBQ, 97 of 143 model-by-category scores are significant and 94 aligned, while the commercial reference abstains on 99.5% of ambiguous items, hiding aligned probability mass. Option swaps flip 0.0% to 72.6% of choices; typed scoring stays

translated_title: 交换、复现、读取概率质量：一种用于审计“系统一”决策模型中人口统计学偏差的协议
translated_abstract: “系统一”决策模型用类型化的、带概率评分的答案取代了文本生成，并正在进入生产环境。这些答案在无人在环的情况下执行，且目前尚无在成熟偏见基准上进行的多模型审计。我们提供了这样的审计：涵盖三个基准（BBQ 的全部十一个类别、CrowS-Pairs 和 SilverSpoon），并将其适配到类型化接口；测试了十二个模型以及一个“无思考”消融配置；共计 1,638,000 个决策。每个顺序敏感的项目都运行两次并交换选项位置；原生类型化模型还会交换标签；十个配置在额外随机种子和批次大小 16 的条件下重复运行。我们发现存在广泛的刻板印象对齐、依赖顺序的答案，以及追踪不稳定性而非偏见的置信度。在 BBQ 中，143 个“模型×类别”评分中有 97 个显著，其中 94 个呈现对齐；而作为商业参考的模型在 99.5% 的模糊项目上选择弃权，从而隐藏了对齐的概率质量。选项交换使 0.0% 至 72.6% 的选择发生翻转；类型化评分保持在……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了首个针对“系统一”决策模型的人口偏见多模型审计协议，基于三个偏见基准、十二个模型共163.8万次决策，发现这些模型普遍存在刻板印象对齐和顺序依赖性，且其置信度反映的是不稳定性而非偏见本身。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the first multi-model audit protocol for demographic bias in System One decision models, conducting 1,638,000 decisions across three benchmarks and twelve models, revealing widespread stereotype alignment, order-dependent answers, and confidence that tracks instability rather than bias.
